## Intent

Research a long-form Anth.us article on coordinated teams of specialized LLM agents that plan, implement, test, review, and ship software, with humans setting direction and governing high-leverage decisions. Use Grok Bot–style persistent agent teams and PostHog’s software-factory and multi-agent review loops as current examples.

## Preferred term

Use **LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) for software engineering** as the formal umbrella. It matches the exact terminology of a peer-reviewed ACM TOSEM systematic review, while FIPA/IEEE and current platform documentation consistently use multi-agent systems or multi-agent collaboration.

## Alternate and discovery terms

- multi-agent software development
- multi-agent collaboration
- multi-agent orchestration
- multi-agent software development framework
- AI agent team / agent team
- coding-agent team
- AI-native software engineering team
- team of always-on agents
- AI teammates
- team of Bots
- agent swarm / coding-agent swarm / QA swarm
- agentic software engineering
- agentic software engineering system
- autonomous software development
- autonomous software development pipeline
- software factory
- AI software factory
- agentic software factory
- lights-off software factory
- dark software factory
- bot farm
- model zoo

## Terminology boundaries

These terms are not exact synonyms. A software factory is the broader end-to-end production operating model and an overloaded metaphor; PostHog explicitly says it has no fixed criteria. An agent swarm usually implies a large, dynamic, or decentralized multi-agent subtype. Orchestration is the coordination layer. Agentic software engineering is a broader discipline and can include single-agent systems. Bot farm commonly means mass-operated fake or spam accounts and carries an abuse connotation. Model zoo means a catalog of pretrained models, not a collaborating team.

## Research questions for the next stage

Compare supervisor-led hierarchies with decentralized handoffs; fixed specialists with dynamically formed teams; shared memory and communication; isolated workspaces; planning, implementation, testing, peer review, CI/CD, and production feedback loops; human-in-the-loop governance; and quality, security, observability, cost, evaluation, and failure modes.

## Starting sources

- ACM TOSEM systematic review: https://doi.org/10.1145/3712003
- FIPA abstract architecture for intentional multi-agent systems: https://www.fipa.org/specs/fipa00001/XC00001J.html
- Grok Bot team collaboration: https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/chat-and-collaboration
- Grok Bot engineering-team example: https://x.ai/bot/guides/grok-bot-for-pms
- PostHog software-factory framing: https://newsletter.posthog.com/p/software-factories
- PostHog multi-agent QA swarm: https://newsletter.posthog.com/p/code-review-tips
- ChatDev, ACL 2024: https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.810/
payload.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Software Engineering
